beats.name: Welcome & choose
beats.where: Welcome to the Directive Tutorial! Step 1 of 7.
beats.about:
Directive is the shared path for building with AI — so a later sitting can continue from the same place instead of starting over.

This practice sitting takes about 10 minutes. You pick one toy project; each option teaches the same path. Nothing here pushes to GitHub.

1. Signal — a tiny CLI that prints your personal status line
2. Postcard — a one-page local site that shows a short message
3. Echo — a mini bot that answers one question with a reply you choose
4. Leave — pause for now (progress is saved; you can start again later)
5. Discuss
6. Back — not available yet (use Leave or Discuss)
beats.caveat: Name and preferences stay in setup. This sitting does not ask those again.

beats.name: Write it down
beats.about:
First, pick the toy content {name} should use. Then we will write the plan down so it is not stuck in this chat.

Example: {contentExample}
beats.caveat: Writing it down is not permission to build yet.
beats.next:
{contentPrompt}

1. Use the example
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back
beats.nextAfterPlan:
Do Plan and Done look right?

1. Yes
2. No — change the plan
3. Leave
4. Discuss
5. Back
beats.nextAfterWorkPending:
Next I'll write the proposed work file and save its path.

1. Leave
2. Discuss
3. Back

beats.name: Confirm & start
beats.about: You are about to approve this one work item and start it. After you say yes, the work moves from proposed to ready, then into progress on its own branch so the change stays reviewable and easy to undo. Owned files for this item: {ownedFiles}.
beats.caveat: Saying yes starts the work. This practice project stays on this machine — no GitHub push and no pull request.
beats.next:
Ready to confirm and start?

1. Yes
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back

beats.name: Make the change
beats.about: Time to build. I will change only what this work owns so {name} does its one job with your content. Nothing else.
beats.caveat: Do not add a second feature or a pull request. Only change {ownedFilesChange}.
beats.next:
Ready for me to write the files and run the local test?

1. Go
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back

beats.name: Prove it
beats.about: Now I will run Directive's acceptance check. It reads the acceptance sentence on the work file and reports whether the result matches.
beats.caveat: A green local test only means your own test passed. The acceptance check is separate.
beats.next:
Run the acceptance check?

1. Go
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back
beats.nextAfterCheckPass:
The acceptance check verified.

1. Continue
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back
beats.nextAfterCheckFail:
The acceptance check did not verify. Stay on this step, fix the mismatch, and run the same check again.

1. Try again
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back

beats.name: Close
beats.about: Record acceptance proof on the work file, then mark the work finished only after the acceptance sentence was verified. Then the work list for this practice sitting is empty.
beats.next:
Complete the work item?

1. Go
2. Leave
3. Discuss
4. Back

beats.name: Wrap up
beats.about:
You walked the same path a real project uses: write the plan down, start on a branch, build, check, and close. Real delivery also includes GitHub, review, and merge — not taught here. You can re-run this tutorial anytime.

Next up: set up your real project.
beats.caveat: This sitting does not publish the project or open a pull request.
beats.next: You are done with this tutorial.
